payload.name: O on Cu(111)
payload.structure_source: ASE fcc111 slab built from MACE-relaxed fcc Cu (a0=3.640 A)
payload.rationale: Atomic O adsorption on Cu(111), most stable site, isolated-O-atom reference (task 0bc70eb6).

_fulfilled_need.query: Compute the adsorption energy of atomic oxygen on Cu(111) at its most stable site, referenced to an isolated O atom.

summary: candidate O on Cu(111) (metal surface adsorbate, trust tier)

method.protocol: 0 K static relaxation (BFGS, fmax 0.01 eV/A); E_ads = E(slab+O) - E(slab) - E(O atom, isolated, 20 A box); fcc/hcp/top/bridge starting sites; bottom half of slab fixed
method.slab: Cu(111) p(3x3), 4 layers, 10 A vacuum each side, 1/9 ML O; convergence checks p(2x2)/p(4x4) 4 layers and p(3x3) 5 layers

payload.note: Most stable site = fcc hollow: fcc -4.837, hcp -4.783, top -3.082 eV (p3x3, 4 layers); a bridge start relaxes into fcc, so bridge is not a minimum. Cu-O = 1.90 A. Convergence: p(4x4) -4.845, p(3x3) 5 layers -4.838, p(2x2) (1/4 ML) -4.904 eV, so numerical error is about 0.01 eV at <=1/9 ML. Same slabs referenced to 1/2 O2 (MACE): -1.69 eV. PREMISE: a well-defined 0 K electronic adsorption energy (no ZPE). The isolated-O energy is never predicted by the network; it equals the model's E0 (-1.548 eV). This is meaningful only because MACE foundation-model E0s are spin-polarized PBE isolated-atom energies. That is consistent with an independent VASP-PBE spin-polarized O atom (-1.531 eV, arXiv 2604.13897). VALIDATION (same setup): bulk Cu a0 3.640 A vs experiment ~3.615 A (+0.7%, typical PBE); Cu cohesive energy 3.50 eV vs experiment ~3.49 eV (this exercises the isolated-atom reference path); O2 De 6.29 eV vs experiment ~5.2 eV. The model reproduces the known PBE O2 overbinding of ~1 eV. Literature DFT anchor: one PBE-type study found by web search reports fcc -5.00 / hcp -4.91 eV vs O atom (Sci China Phys Mech Astron, doi 10.1007/s11433-012-4868-5, not independently re-read), 0.16 eV more binding than this result; fcc preference agrees. UNCERTAINTY +/-0.3 eV covers MLIP-vs-PBE error for an out-of-training-distribution surface+adsorbate (MPtrj/sAlex are mostly bulk), spread between DFT setups, and slab convergence. It does NOT cover the error of PBE itself vs the true (experimental) value. For an atom-referenced O binding energy that error may be several tenths of an eV (overbinding), as the O2 test shows. No direct experimental value referenced to the O atom was used.

summary: O on Cu(111) adsorption_energy = -4.84 eV via ALCHEMI env / ASE 3.29 + mace-torch 0.3.15 (GPU, float64)/MACE-MPA-0 medium (macempa0mediummodel) 0 K static relaxation (BFGS, fmax 0.01 eV/A); E_ads = E(slab+O) - E(slab) - E(O atom, isolated, 20 A box); fcc/hcp/top/bridge starting sites; bottom half of slab fixed
